entries.summary: New files: `common/src/ads/web-agentic-offer.ts`, `common/src/desktop-cloud/project-secrets.ts`.

ai.title: Add web agentic offer, cloud execution, tool releases, and project
ai.summary: The `common` package gains a new module, `web-agentic-offer.ts`, which allows the Cloud worker to build a sponsored run capability from a browser workspace worktree without a local client inspection, while `sponsored-execution-surface.ts` adds `cloud_linux` as a server-assigned execution surface that no client may claim on the wire. The sponsored skill format in `sponsored-skill.ts` extends `path` tools with optional checksummed release archives (pinned by SHA-256, limited to 4 assets per tool) so the web harness can install vendor CLIs, and a new `sponsoredSkillWebRefusal` function blocks skills lacking `linux` or needing already-installed `path` tools from running on web. Additionally, `common/src/desktop-cloud/project-secrets.ts` introduces sealed project-level environment variables that drop into every chat shell, with reserved names (including `FREEBUFF_*` and `NODE_OPTIONS`) rejected to prevent hijacking.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/ads/web-agentic-offer.ts` defines `WEB_CAPABILITY_COMMAND` and `cloudSponsoredCapability`; `common/src/ads/sponsored-execution-surface.ts` adds `SPONSORED_CLOUD_EXECUTION_SURFACE` ('cloud_linux') and `SPONSORED_ACCEPT_SURFACES` now includes 'web'; `common/src/ads/sponsored-skill.ts` introduces `SponsoredSkillToolRelease` types for vendor CLI installation; `common/src/desktop-cloud/project-secrets.ts` adds sealed project environment variables.
ai.unknowns: The specific rollout mechanism for enabling `web` in `SPONSORED_ACCEPT_SURFACES` and the consumer of the new project secrets API are not shown in this diff.

changes.what: New `web-agentic-offer.ts` module and `cloud_linux` execution surface enable browser workspace sponsored runs
Sponsored skill format extended with vendor CLI release archives and web refusal logic
New sealed project secrets module with reserved variable name validation

eli5.text: The ad system now supports a new way to run sponsored tasks directly inside a web browser workspace on a Linux virtual machine, rather than on a user's local computer. A new security rule ensures that project-level environment variables used by these web tasks cannot override critical system settings, preventing a project from hijacking the assistant's behavior. This is an internal infrastructure update to the ad-serving pipeline that prepares the system for future browser-based sponsored tasks; it does not change how you interact with the assistant or your coding sessions today.

ai.title: Add project key field to agentic offer request schema
ai.summary: The `agenticOfferRequestSchema` in `common/src/ads/agentic-offer.ts` now accepts an optional `projectKey` field. This field identifies the conversation's project, formatted as `local:<sha256 prefix>`, or null for a chat with no folder. The comment specifies that agentic relevance reads the project's understanding profile, and that the value is parsed with `parseAdRequestProjectKey`, so a malformed value is dropped instead of failing the request. This integrates project-specific context into the agentic offer decision flow alongside the existing `traceContext` field.

ai.title: Document bun test module mock persistence and file order
ai.summary: The testing guide adds a detailed section explaining that `mock.module()` in bun test persists for the rest of the process and cannot be undone by `mock.restore()`. It identifies `clearMockedModules()` from `@codebuff/common/testing/mock-modules.ts` as the only mechanism to reset module mocks. The section further explains that Bun traverses test directories breadth-first, meaning test execution order depends on filesystem readdir order rather than command-line argument order, which affects how module mocks leak between test files.

ai.title: Count the review-mode file edit tool in the file edit loop guard
ai.summary: The file edit loop guard in the agent runtime now recognizes the review-mode file edit tool as part of the loop detection. Previously, repeated rejections of this tool were not tracked by the guard, so a model could spin on the same failing proposal without triggering the recovery or stop thresholds. The tool list was updated to match the fact that this tool produces the same rejection result shape as the standard string replace tool. New tests assert that a streak of identical rejected proposals now counts toward the loop limit.
ai.evidence: In `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/file-edit-loop.ts`, the `FILE_EDIT_LOOP_TOOL_NAMES` array was expanded to include the review-mode editor tool, and the updated docblock notes that the tool builds the same rejection result as the standard string replace tool and was previously uncounted.

eli5.text: The safety check that stops the assistant from endlessly repeating the same failed file edit now also counts a specific review-mode editing tool. Previously, this tool could get stuck in a loop without triggering the automatic stop, wasting time on repeated failures. You will notice fewer long, unproductive waiting periods when the assistant struggles with a tricky code change, as it reaches the stop point faster. This small improvement applies to anyone using the assistant and does not require any action on your part.
